text:
alex: Quick sync - we need to pick a path for attribute bloat. telemetry ingest up 38% week-over-week; most of it is large attrs like graphql.resolve.input and sdk.metadata. do we minify on ingest or keep everything and pay the cost?
maria: clarify goal: reduce storage costs vs improve query latency for customers? those pull in different solutions.
ajex: both, but immediate pressure is ingest/storage. long-term customer queries also suffer when large maps are scanned. example: some customers attach entire user profiles under request.user.
jevon: proposal: policy-based minify. keep full attrs for errors & slow traces, minify for normal samples. also route-level overrides for important endpoints.
sara: agree on policy. also suggest soft-minify: store small preview + hash pointer so we can rehydrate on-demand (behind auth & billing).
maria: can you sketch pseudocode for minify transform so infra can cost it out?
jevon: pseudocode:

for attr in trace.attrs:
  if is_large(attr.value):
    out.minified[attr.key] = summarize(attr.value)  // len, type, sha256
    out.preview[attr.key] = truncate(attr.value, 256)
  else:
    out[attr.key] = attr.value

we keep preview (256 bytes) + sha256 pointer to full stored blob that is only retrievable via rehydrate API.

ops-bot: deploy-preview: feature/attr-minify will canary at 09:10 UTC :rocket:
alex: decision axes: 1) aggressiveness (truncate vs drop keys) 2) retention tiers (route/customer/error) 3) rehydrate UX and billing.
maria: tradeoffs: more aggressive => fewer debug signals. route-level retention needs ownership + mapping.
sara: ops complexity: rehydrate requires auth checks, audit logs; also adds tail latency for retrieval. need a billing plan for rehydrations.
alex: can we rollout by payload size? e.g., minify traces with payload >10KB or token_count >1000.
jevon: yes, gateway already computes payload_size. rollout plan suggestion:
- week1: minify non-error traces >10KB for 10% of customers
- week2: expand to 50% + enable per-route override UI
- week3: enable hash-based rehydrate via billing portal
maria: what about eval infra? we compare runs and need consistent attributes.
sara: add attrs_truncated=true flag on traces so evals can exclude or treat them specially.
alex: infra changes needed:
- ingest transform hook (minify)
- retention policy config (route/customer/error)
- rehydrate service with auth + audit logs
- console UI showing attrs_truncated + rehydrate button (costed action)
jevon: rough estimate: ingest storage down ~25%, query CPU down ~15% after removing large fields.
maria: action items:
- jevon: PR for ingest transform + unit tests (due Tue)
- sara: design rehydrate API + auth flow (due Wed)
- alex/infra: coordinate canary deploy
alex: decision for now: implement policy-based minify with conservative thresholds (truncate to 256 bytes, keep sha256 pointer). rollout to 10% of non-error traces first. set attrs_truncated flag.
maria: ack. please file a short RFC summary and link here when PRs land.
jevon: will open PR and link when ready, adding unit tests for nested maps and binary blobs.
sara: will add rehydrate API spec to docs and public FAQ explaining billing for rehydration.
alex: thanks all. ping if tracing dashboards regress during canary. :thumbsup:
